lines.text: A man is loading boxes into a dusty pickup truck. He stops dead at the sight of me, like he'd memorized every face in town and mine doesn't fit.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: You new around here? I... I don't see new faces too often.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: My car broke down on the highway. I'm staying a night at the motel.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: The motel. Sure. Good luck with that.
He says it like a bitter joke he's got no plans to explain. He goes back to loading boxes without looking at me again.

topics.displayName: Ask about his shop and last night

lines.text: The crumpled receipt with Robert's debt note is in my notebook. I bring it up in passing.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: What about it? A bad month. Two. People don't buy good carpet anymore, they buy cheap synthetic rolls.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: I don't know why you're snooping around my business. I was doing delivery runs... had nothing to do with what happened behind the motel.
Nobody mentioned the motel alley. He brings it up himself, visibly sweating.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: The shop is what it is. Not much of a life, but it's mine.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: Used to sell well. Now people just speed by. And with what happened at the motel, things are only getting tighter.
He talks about the shop like he's talking about himself — trapped by circumstances he can't escape.
I show him the synthetic olive-green fiber found by the splinters near the alley.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: That proves nothing. I sell that carpet weave all over the county.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You claimed you were locked in your shop all night, but your truck was seen circling the back alley at midnight.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: I was making late runs! Checking on property! Is that a crime now?
He nervously clutches his right palm. A jagged, fresh cut peeks out from under a filthy bandage.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: And that cut?

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: A metal trim! Cut myself moving boxes in the dark. You can't pin a murder on a working man just for being broke!
He breathes heavily, terrified of taking the blame for a crime he only helped clean up.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You said you were closing up the shop alone all night.

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: Yeah. That's what happened. What else do you want from me?
He crosses his arms tightly, hiding his bandaged palm.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: And that hand?

lines.speaker: Ernesto
lines.text: A can. Nothing. We done here?
Without physical proof linking him to the scene, he keeps his guard up.
